newsitem.title: USA: Mercury Finance holders sue directors, KPMG.
newsitem.headline: Mercury Finance holders sue directors, KPMG.

text.p: Three Mercury Finance Co shareholders have sued the directors of the company and its auditors, KPMG Peat Marwick LLP, for alleged breach of fiduciary duty for failure to disclose material information.

Late on Tuesday, Doran Malone and Joseph and Adrienne Danielle filed an individual and class action complaint in the Delaware Chancery Court alleging "wrongdoing committed by the directors" and unspecified "aiding and abetting."

"The filing Mercury has made with the Securities and Exchange Commission and every communication to the stockholders for the last three years have been materially false" including "overstatements of Mercury's earnings," court papers say.
"Specifically, Mercury has now admitted that (its) earnings for 1996 were only $56.7 million...rather than the $120.7 million...as disclosed by the directors," the papers say.

Mercury stock lost about 86 percent of its value last week after it was forced to restate its 1996 earnings due to accounting irregularities. On Monday, company officials in Chicago met with lenders to discuss financing arrangements to meet liquidity needs.
Other class action lawsuits by Mercury shareholders were filed Friday and earlier this week in federal courts in Illinois. They allege that Mercury overstated its earnings.
The complete complaint document in the Chancery Court action will not be made available until it has been served on the defendants.
Mercury Finance Corp is not a named defendant. No other information on the lawsuit is available at this time.
